shortDescription: Wage growth in Poland, closely watched by the central bank for its effect on inflation, slowed more than expected in August, data showed on Monday.

children: Wage growth in Poland, closely watched by the central bank for its effect on inflation, slowed more than expected in August, data showed on Monday.
The Statistics Office reported that wage growth (PLWAGE=ECI) came in at 5.6% last month, below the 6.4% forecast by analysts. In monthly terms, wages fell by 2.6%.
Corporate employment (PLEMPY=ECI) fell 0.8% year-on-year, in line with market expectations.
"Wage pressure remains subdued, with the main risk factor for inflation being the external energy shock," ING analysts wrote in a commentary.

Wage data are closely monitored by the central bank for their impact on inflation, which accelerated to 3.4% year-on-year in August from 3.0% in July, just below the 3.5% upper limit of the inflation target range.
"This picture of the labour market is favourable from the perspective of the Monetary Policy Council," said PKO BP.

The National Bank of Poland kept its main interest rate at 3.75% on September 9, maintaining its cautious approach as rising commodity prices and increased energy costs create a risk of higher inflation.
